key_insight: CoRe-WM learns how breast MRI states evolve during treatment, then uses frozen representations to predict pathologic complete response (pCR).
clinical_relevance: Tracking evolving imaging response could improve pCR risk estimates during neoadjuvant chemotherapy, though clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Predicts the next latent imaging state from longitudinal DCE-MRI.
Conditions state transitions on patient clinical profiles and assigned therapy.
Separates morphology-focused response dynamics from imaging appearance, then predicts pCR with a linear readout.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports the highest discrimination among evaluated methods at every assessed decision point in five-fold I-SPY2 cross-validation, plus robust transfer to I-SPY1, without numerical metrics.
watch_item: Prospective validation is needed to establish whether predictions improve treatment decisions or patient outcomes.
paper_title: CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI
